review_list.name: Tūpare
review_list.reason: For: historic free garden with Wikipedia article, tourism board names it. Against: one counted source, mainly seasonal bloom.

review_list.name: Pouākai Circuit
review_list.reason: For: Wikivoyage Egmont NP lists the 2-3 day circuit; multi-day walks a guide promotes qualify. Against: one source, overlaps Pouākai Crossing and Tarns already in the app.

review_list.name: Curtis Falls Track
review_list.reason: For: DOC lists the track to a waterfall. Against: one source (DOC page fetch showed little detail), short walk within a park already covered.

review_list.name: Brooklands Zoo
review_list.reason: For: Wikivoyage lists a small free zoo, permanent, about an hour with kids. Against: one counted source, small local zoo.

review_list.name: TSB Bank Bowls New Zealand Museum
review_list.reason: For: Wikivoyage names the world's only lawn bowls museum; quirky, permanent. Against: one source, niche, small, opening unverified.

review_list.name: Hollard Gardens
review_list.reason: For: tourism board lists it among Taranaki's gardens (Gardens of National Significance). Against: one source, small, South Taranaki.

review_list.name: Taranaki Pioneer Village
review_list.reason: For: tourism board Stratford page names a 1850-1950 pioneer village museum, a permanent half-day visit. Against: one source, opening days unverified (may be limited days).

review_list.name: Turuturu Mokai Pā
review_list.reason: For: Wikivoyage names the public pā reserve near Hāwera, beside Tawhiti Museum. Against: one source, small heritage site, ~20-30 minute look.

review_list.name: Te Maire Loop Track
review_list.reason: For: tourism board names a 2-hour forest loop with a suspension bridge. Against: one source, no coordinates found, little detail.

review_list.name: Matemateaonga Track
review_list.reason: For: multi-day backcountry track named by the tourism board (DOC-managed walkway); multi-day walks qualify. Against: one source, remote, little visitor use, no coordinates.

benchmark.applicable: Taranaki holds none of the named benchmark places (Red Rocks, Kapiti, Coleridge, Christchurch, Glenorchy, Hump Ridge, St Kilda, Ohakune Carrot, Ninety Mile Beach, TSS Earnslaw).
benchmark.negative_benchmarks_honoured: Vehicles/operators rejected (Chaddy's Charters, Precision Helicopters, Forgotten World Adventures); minor memorials rejected (Ambury, Joshua Morgan); once-a-week/occasional venues rejected (New Plymouth Model Railway, Observatory); events rejected (WOMAD, Festival of Lights, Republic Day); local parks rejected (King Edward Park x2).
benchmark.gateway_village_check: Whangamōmona is the Pipiriki analogue (the candidate note itself says its draw is the journey beyond it). The benchmark expects such a village in review; the skeptic kept it as a quirky icon (1989 'republic', historic hotel). Placed as a proposed destination hub with Moki Tunnel and Mount Damper Falls, flagged for the owner; if the owner prefers review, the two spots become standalone.

flags_for_owner: Ōakura village (5010 views) rejected by the skeptic as a duplicate of Ōakura Beach (kept); Waimoku is placed with New Plymouth although DOC lists Kaitake within the park.
Waitara (7259) and Inglewood (5264) left out: Wikivoyage region-list mentions only, no named thing to do (fails 'What qualifies' 1).
Cape Egmont Lighthouse is a single-source landmark kept as marginal by the skeptic.
Stratford, Hāwera, Ōpunake, Whangamōmona are proposals only; Ōpunake and Whangamōmona have just two spots each.
